newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan ministry to sell $225 mln China Steel share.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan ministry to sell $225 mln China Steel share.

text.p: Taiwan's economics ministry said on Wednesday it would sell shares in China Steel worth T$6.27 billion (US$225 million), furthering a selloff of firms formerly or still controlled by the state.

"We expect to release 214 million China Steel shares before the end of July," a spokesman of the ministry's Commission of National Corporations told Reuters by telephone after the close of trading on Wednesday.
The commission would choose an underwriter through open bidding to issue the shares, the spokesman added.
The release would reduce state ownership in China Steel to 39 percent from 42 percent and was the next step in a five-year process to sell the state's entire China Steel stake, he said.
At China Steel's current price, the auction would net some T$6.27 billion for the national treasury, brokers said.

China Steel lost T$0.4 to close at T$29.3 on Wednesday as investors, who got wind of the selloff through local media, sold their holdings in anticipation of a flood of China Steel shares in the market, brokers said.
China Steel, Taiwan's largest steel firm, was privatised in April 1995. In February, it released 225 million shares through issuance of global depositary receipts overseas.
